subject: On‑prem nightly batch: sudden throughput collapse — exec sync & mitigation request

From: Acme Robotics Ops <ops+infra@acme-robotics.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly batch: 60% drop in inference throughput on our private cluster

Hi David / Laura,

We hit a severe degradation during our nightly reconciliation batch that started at 00:30 local time and lasted ~90 minutes. Throughput for model 'rwd-latest-quant' on our on‑prem VPC dropped ~60% and p95 token latency jumped from ~320ms to ~1.4s. We saw a cascade ofdecoder 502s in the logs and requests backed up in the broker queue.

We're attaching the flight log and a heap snapshot we were asked to capture. This is causing downstream scorecard jobs to miss SLAs — this is high priority. Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Attachments: nightly_batch_flight_log.csv, heap_profile_030328.txt

—Rachel (on behalf of Acme Ops)

Subject: Re: Nightly batch: 60% drop in inference throughput on our private cluster

Quick triage notes after an initial pass through the flight log and heap profile:

- Broker queue shows steady enqueue rate but a sudden drop in dequeue throughput at 00:33; worker processes were saturated in cpu wait/IO wait.
- GPU-side traces show intermittent CUDA kernel timeouts correlated with a spike in small‑sequence warmups (batch size variance).
- Heap snapshot indicates a spike in metadata allocations around the KV cache index shuffle — likely related to a compaction/rehash that ran at the same time as the batch window.

Immediate mitigations we recommend (can be executed in parallel):
1) Temporarily enable our smaller quantized variant (rwd-latest-q4) as a fallback for batch calls to reduce kernel time.
2) Increase broker consumers by +2 for the batch window and reduce the per‑worker max_batch_size to smooth variance.
3) Disable scheduled KV cache compaction during the batch window (config flag: runtime.cache.compaction.enabled=false).
4) Collect a GPU kernel timeline and broker thread dump for the 00:30–00:40 window.

Priyom — can you take ownership of implementing 1 and 2 with Acme's consent? David / Laura — we should also consider a short exec sync if enabling fallback or scaling requires a contract exception.

—Marissa
Sr. SRE, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Hi Rachel,

We can implement the following immediately if you approve:
- Flip runtime flag to route batch calls to rwd-latest-q4 fallback for the next 3 runs (no model version pin required).
- Spin up 2 additional broker consumers for the nightly window and set max_batch_size from 64 -> 48 to reduce kernel variability.

Expected short‑term impact: should bring p95 back to ~400–500ms and clear the backlog within two batch cycles. There will be small quality delta for a subset of requests; we'll surface sample outputs to your team for signoff.

Please reply with APPROVE and approximate time window when you'd like us to make the change. If we don't hear back in 30 minutes we'll prepare the change in a paused state and execute on explicit confirmation.

—Priyom
Platform Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
